title: SharePoint admin center: item-level report on Everyone and Everyone except external users permissions
summary: The report's navigation, PowerShell command, licensing conditions and operational limits are supported by Microsoft documentation, and its release details match the roadmap. A minor checklist-to-controls-table mismatch remains for role assignment, the prerequisite report and remediation.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups is a SharePoint Advanced Management Data access governance snapshot report.
claims.quote: The Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups report is one of the Data access governance snapshot reports available with SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report gives exact item-level permission details where Everyone except external users or Everyone is the recipient, subject to the stated exclusions and download limit.
claims.quote: This report provides exact item-level permission details for every item where the special SharePoint groups Everyone except external users (EEEU) or Everyone are the recipients.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report is admin-opt-in: an administrator runs it on demand, rather than the report changing existing permissions on arrival.
claims.quote: A Global administrator must assign the SharePoint Advanced Admin role before you can run this report. Select Run report under either Content shared with 'Everyone' group or Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The report is run in SharePoint admin center through Reports > Data access governance > Snapshot reports > Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups > View reports > Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group > Run report.
claims.quote: Under Snapshot reports, in the Sites and files shared via special SharePoint groups section, select View reports. Select Run report under either Content shared with 'Everyone' group or Content shared with 'Everyone except external users' group.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsers -ReportType Snapshot generates the detailed EEEU report in Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsers -ReportType Snapshot
The above cmdlet generates a detailed report for all content shared with 'Everyone except external users' (Sites, groups and files) across both SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Using -ReportEntity Everyone with -ReportType Snapshot generates the Everyone report.
claims.quote:
To generate the report for Everyone, change the ReportEntity parameter value:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity Everyone -ReportType Snapshot

claims.quote: This report requires module Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell version 16.0.27215.12000 or later, published April 30, 2026.

claims.claim: The report downloads as a ZIP file containing a CSV.
claims.quote: Select Download report on the report for the group you want. The download is a ZIP file that contains a CSV file listing all items where that group has direct or indirect access.

claims.quote: The identifier columns form a hierarchy, from your organization down to the individual item, which lets you pivot or summarize across a specific identifier.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The CSV identifies the permission level granted.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Everyone inside Style Resource Readers on classic publishing sites is an example of an excluded permission.
claims.quote: For example, the report doesn't include the Everyone group inside the Style Resource Readers group. In classic publishing site templates, the Style Resource Readers group controls read permissions for the Master Page Gallery and restricted access to the Style Library.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The existing site permissions report identifies overshared sites, whereas this report identifies the items and how access was granted.
claims.quote: While the site permissions for your organization report tells you which sites are overshared, this report tells you exactly which items are overshared and how access was granted

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft positions the report as a basis for scripted cleanup rather than relying on individual site owners.
claims.quote: Use this report when you want to find exactly where oversharing happens in your organization and fix it through scripting, rather than depending on individual site owners to review and modify permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The content being reported is already visible to every internal user through these groups.
claims.quote: Content shared with these groups is visible to every internal user

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says content shared with these groups surfaces directly in Microsoft Copilot search results.
claims.quote: Content shared with these groups is visible to every internal user, and it surfaces directly in Microsoft Copilot search results

claims.where: Why it matters
